<span class="origin-badge origin-badge--onesimus">Onesimus extension</span>

Direct children of one directory of a job chain (OVFS).

## Synopsis

```text
.ovfs_ls [jobid=<jobid>[,...]] [client=<client>] [fileset=<fileset>]
         path=<path> [json]
```

Words without brackets are required, `[ ]` marks optional parts, `a | b` alternatives, `...` a repeatable argument and `[,...]` a comma separated list.

## Description

Onesimus extension: lists the direct entries of one directory in the state of a job chain, first the files, then the subdirectories with the number of their entries, so a restore browser can load the tree directory by directory. Directories below which nothing can be restored are left out. The chain is given by jobid= or by client= (and fileset=) for the newest state; path= is required and ends with a slash.

Each entry carries its restore identity (jobid, fileindex). json prints the result as one JSON line in every API mode.

## Arguments {#arguments}

| Argument | Type | Values / source | Default | Flags | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jobid=` | string |  |  | list | Job ID list. |
| `client=` | resource | from [`.clients`](../dot-clients/) |  |  | Client name (latest state). |
| `fileset=` | resource | from [`.filesets`](../dot-filesets/) |  |  | FileSet name. |
| `path=` | string |  |  | required | Directory. |
| `json` | keyword |  |  |  | Print the JSON object as text. |

## Examples

The entries of /etc in a job chain:

```text
.ovfs_ls jobid=600,615,616 path=/etc/
```

A directory of the newest state as JSON:

```text
.ovfs_ls client=bareos-fd path=/home/ json
```
